rules.quote: Use the right writing style. For example, instructions and transactions are more direct and use the imperative. Reports of events usually use the past tense of the verb.
rules.specification: Instructions and transaction steps should use imperative verbs. Event reports should use past tense verbs.
rules.violation_condition: instructions or transactional steps written without using imperative mood verbs, or reports of events written without using past tense verbs
when: Writing instructional or transactional content, or reports of events.
rules.why: Specific, actionable grammar/style requirement (imperative for instructions, past tense for event reports) with dedicated compliant examples (G-1, E-1).

examples.note: Example showing consistent heading styles across stages.

rules.quote: Be consistent in the language, style and design of headings at the same level across the content.
rules.specification: Headings at the same hierarchical level within a document or process should follow a consistent grammatical and stylistic pattern.
rules.violation_condition: headings at the same level across a piece of content that use inconsistent language, grammatical phrasing, or styling
rules.why: G-5 vs text rule: 'Be consistent in the language, style and design of headings at the same level across the content' is an actionable structural rule about text headings.
